analysis.summary: Creates a relic near a plot and places it in the nearest relic slot.

notes.text: Calls GetNearestRelicSlot for the plot (returns a city plus building type and slot), then Game::Culture::AddRelic. If that returns a valid great work, it looks up the slot's work and sends a Reporting event (hash 0x1a71e9f0).

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: **If `GetNearestRelicSlot` finds no free relic slot, the function does nothing at all**: no relic is chosen, no record is created, no event is sent. (The relic is chosen inside `AddRelic`, which is only called when a slot exists.) This is the "relic lost when slots are full" behavior.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Direct callers (13): the combat resolvers (`ResolveMeleeUnitVsUnitCombat` and siblings, `AttackInto`), `Map::Player::Visibility::Manager::ViewPlotContents`, `Unit::Commands::SpreadDissent::Start`, and `GameEffects::Effects::GrantRelic::Apply` (a modifier effect). All relic sources funnel through this one function. Which caller is the goody hut, apostle death or city-state perk is inferred from the names, not verified.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Any notification or era score a player sees when the slots are full is produced by the caller or another system, not by this function or `AddRelic` (which only announce on success). (Medium; not traced.)

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Relics use the same slot machinery as other great works (AddRelic reaches AddGreatWorkToSlot). (Medium.)

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: A bridge between religion and the great work slot system; worth reading alongside the great works topic.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: With the stock DLL and every relic slot full, calling CreateRelic left the game-wide great work record count unchanged: the relic is never created (it stays in the pool), it is not created and thrown away.

evidence.note: Observed in-game (2026-09-30, single player)

notes.text: A hook that, for a human player with no free relic slot, calls AddRelic with an out-of-range slot instead creates the record and archives the relic: confirmed with the `hut xN` test command (the Palace holds one relic slot; relics were archived only once it was full).

analysis.summary: Re-homes a list of great works after a building replacement changes a city's slots.

notes.text: For each work in the list: if the city's own Buildings can take it (`CanAddGreatWork`), it adds it there via `edit()` + `AddGreatWork`.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Otherwise it walks the player's other cities and, for every other city where `CanAddGreatWork` is true, calls `AddGreatWork`.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: If no city can take it, nothing happens: no notification, no record, no fallback. The work simply ends up in no slot.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: The loop over other cities has no `break`/`return` after a successful add.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: A work that fits nowhere is silently dropped from all slots (it probably still exists in the game-wide great work list). (Medium.)

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Because the loop does not stop after the first successful add, the same work could be added to more than one other city if `CanAddGreatWork` only checks the target city and not other cities. **Possible duplication bug. (Low: depends on what `CanAddGreatWork` checks, not yet read.)**

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: One concrete way works "get lost": a building replacement with no spare slots elsewhere. The work is neither archived nor reported.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Relevant to any 'great works archive' idea: this is a point where a work could be saved instead of dropped.

analysis.summary: Adds a (possibly negative) amount to a unit's remaining build charges, never going below 0.

notes.text: Current charges are at unit+0x538. New value = current + delta, clamped to 0.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Assigns through a tracked variable (CopyAssignmentDo on a FAutoVariable at unit+0x528).

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: If delta != 0, sends a Reporting event (hash 0xb2176dc4) carrying the new and old values.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: The event is likely what refreshes the UI's charge display. (Medium.)

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: A small, self-contained mutator with no documented Lua equivalent. Clamping and the event come for free if this function is called instead of writing the field.

evidence.note: decompilation read in Ghidra

notes.text: Address 0x3a2980 in the installed build matched the expected function prologue.

evidence.note: Observed in-game (2026-09-29, vanilla game, single-player, Frida log-only hook)

notes.text: A Builder building an improvement called it with delta = -1; the int at unit+0x538 went from 3 to 2.

evidence.note: Observed in-game (2026-09-29, vanilla game, single-player, Frida log-only hook)

notes.text: Calling it ourselves with delta = +1 (Frida, from inside the game's own call on the game thread) raised the field from 2 to 3 (log: `charges now 3`); the user reported the builder's charges then looked correct in the UI (user-reported, not logged). So the address, the calling convention (this + int), the sign convention and the field at unit+0x538 are confirmed.

evidence.note: Observed in-game (2026-09-29, vanilla game, single-player, Frida log-only hook)

notes.text: Clamp confirmed: calling with delta = -100 on a unit with 2 charges left the field at 0 (log), never negative. A follow-up call with a positive delta restored the intended value.

evidence.note: Observed in-game (2026-09-29, vanilla game, single-player, Frida log-only hook)

notes.text: Bonus test: game spent 1 (2 -> 1), our extra call added +2 (field 3). The unit loses focus after acting; after the user reselected it, the UI showed the higher count (user-reported). So the displayed value follows the field, at least on reselect.

evidence.note: Observed in-game (2026-09-29, vanilla game, single-player, Frida log-only hook)

notes.text: **Exposed to Lua and tested (2026-09-29).** A local build of the Community Extension (upstream master + a ~10-line wrapper, `UnitManager.ChangeBuildCharges(unit, delta)`, offset 0x3a2980) plus a gameplay script that adds one charge to each Builder at the start of the player's turn: in a fresh single-player game Builders regained a charge each turn, as intended (user-reported). Needs a custom GameCore, so the mod is incompatible with other GameCore mods.

evidence.note: Observed in-game (2026-09-29, vanilla game, single-player, Frida log-only hook)

notes.text: Not yet observed: whether the UI updates instantly without reselecting (untestable in this setup because the unit deselects), whether the Reporting event fires for a direct call, and behavior for units other than Builders.
